17708249.summary: The Renewables Infrastructure Group Limited purchased 260,000 ordinary shares on 27 July 2026 at a weighted average price of 76.38p through Investec Bank plc, within its share buyback programme announced in August 2024. The shares will be held in treasury. TRIG now holds 155,022,374 treasury shares, with 2,330,940,512 voting rights outstanding.
17708249.brief: TRIG repurchases 260,000 shares at 76.38p per share under its buyback programme.
17708249.take: Routine share buyback execution consistent with announced programme; modest capital allocation activity with minimal immediate market implications for retail investors.

17708250.summary: Essentra delivered H1 2026 revenue of £166.1m (up 9.8% constant currency), with adjusted operating profit of £18.1m at 10.9% margin. Adjusted basic EPS grew 21.3% to 4.3p. The company completed the Boteco acquisition in June, strengthening machine building and automation capabilities. Management launched a Growth and Simplification programme targeting 150bps adjusted operating margin improvement by 2028, with a new 14% margin milestone on the path to its 18% medium-term target. Net debt stands at £70.7m (1.6x EBITDA). FY26 expectations remain unchanged.
17708250.brief: Essentra posts strong H1 results with 9.8% revenue growth; sets new 14% operating margin target for 2028.
17708250.take: Positive read: strong organic growth across all regions, disciplined cost initiatives underway, and clear margin progression roadmap with realistic 2028 target requiring no major market improvement—supports confidence in mid-term guidance.

17708251.summary: Plus500 Limited purchased 8,942 ordinary shares on 27 July 2026 through Panmure Liberum Limited under its share buyback programme announced 9 February 2026. Shares bought at 3,960-4,024p with volume-weighted average price of 3,998.15p. Company now holds 45,985,244 treasury shares with 68,903,133 shares remaining in issue, representing total voting rights.
17708251.brief: Plus500 repurchased 8,942 shares at 3,960-4,024p as part of ongoing buyback programme.
17708251.take: Routine capital management activity under approved buyback programme; demonstrates confidence in valuation but represents modest share reduction with minimal market impact.

17708252.summary: Sabre Insurance Group PLC purchased 150,000 ordinary shares for cancellation between 23-27 July 2026 under its shareholder-approved buyback programme announced 2 June 2026. Shares were bought at prices ranging from 186.30p to 186.60p via Panmure Liberum Limited on the London Stock Exchange. Following cancellation, the company now has 244,265,931 ordinary shares in issue, representing total voting rights.
17708252.brief: Sabre Insurance completes share buyback, purchasing 150,000 shares at 186.30-186.60p for cancellation.
17708252.take: Routine capital management execution within authorised buyback programme; modest share count reduction slightly accretive to earnings per share but non-event for market given standard buy-back activity.

17708253.summary: Revenue increased 21% to £175.4m (H1 2025: £144.4m) with organic and inorganic growth equally contributing. Adjusted operating profit rose 19% to £29.9m, maintaining 20.1% margin. Adjusted PBT climbed 23% to £22.3m with adjusted basic EPS up 24% to 12.4p. Net debt stood at £122.5m with leverage at 1.7x. Information Management drove growth at 26%, while Technology doubled operating profit. Board confident full-year adjusted PBT will meet market expectations of £47.2m.
17708253.brief: Restore PLC reports strong H1 2026 with 21% revenue growth to £175.4m and 24% adjusted EPS growth to 12.4p.
17708253.take: Strong operational momentum across divisions, improved leverage, and maintained margin expansion suggest market will view this positively; company well-positioned for organic and acquisition-led growth.

17708254.summary: NewRiver achieved 13 consecutive quarters of leasing outperformance vs ERV (+4.0% in Q1, +5.7% core portfolio), with 165,900 sq ft of lettings securing £1.8m annualised rent. Occupancy rose to 95.4% with 96% tenant retention. The company acquired BRAVO's 90% stake in The Moor Sheffield for £38.3m (10% NIY), bringing full ownership and concluding a capital partnership with 21% IRR. A new £240m unsecured facility refinances the secured £140m Mall Facility in January 2027, improving debt structure; proforma LTV stands at 43% against 50% policy.
17708254.brief: NewRiver REIT reports strong Q1 leasing, completes £38.3m Moor Sheffield acquisition, secures £240m unsecured refinancing facility.
17708254.take: Market likely views this positively: consistent leasing momentum, attractive acquisition at discount, improved financing terms and deleveraging path demonstrate operational strength and disciplined capital allocation supporting dividend sustainability.

17708255.summary: GreenRoc Strategic Materials has commenced Phase III drilling at its Amitsoq graphite deposit in South Greenland. The first hole (AM_DD_039), completed 23 July, intersected 9.7m of Lower Graphite Layer ore at expected depth and thickness (107.15-119.51m). The company plans drilling through August, with geotechnical and hydrogeological testing underway to support a Pre-Feasibility Study later this year. Amitsoq holds a 23.05Mt JORC resource at 20.41% graphite grade.
17708255.brief: GreenRoc begins Phase III drilling at Amitsoq graphite project in Greenland; first hole confirms expected ore grades.
17708255.take: Successful confirmation of ore continuity at expected grades represents on-track project development and validates exploration assumptions; positive momentum for a strategically designated EU project with secured financing and licensing in place.

17708240.summary: Revenue increased at least 20% to $23.3m+ in 1H2026 versus $19.4m prior year, driven by art outsourcing demand and contributions from Vertic Studios and Shanghai Mineloader Digital (acquired April 2025). Adjusted EBITDA declined to $1.0-1.3m from $2.4m as the company invested ~$0.4m in North America studio Ampera (acquired April 2026) and ~$0.9m diverting resources to AI-enabled game development capabilities. 2H2026 revenue expected to exceed 1H results with continued investment planned.
17708240.brief: Winking Studios reports 20%+ revenue growth in 1H2026 but EBITDA margin compression due to strategic investments.
17708240.take: Growth trajectory is solid but near-term profitability pressure from M&A integration and capability-building investments may disappoint near-term margin-focused investors, though management frames these as positioning for higher-margin future opportunities.

17708238.summary: Science Group plc bought back 5,000 of its 1p ordinary shares on 27 July 2026 at 583 pence per share, representing 0.01% of voting rights. The shares were purchased through Panmure Liberum Limited and will be held in treasury. Following the transaction, the company has 40,642,593 shares in issue (excluding treasury) and holds 5,543,281 treasury shares.
17708238.brief: Science Group PLC repurchased 5,000 shares at 583p per share on 27 July 2026.
17708238.take: Routine share buyback as part of standard capital management programme; modest scale suggests non-material shareholder value impact.

17708239.summary: Everplay Group traded in line with board expectations in H1 2026, supported by new releases and back catalogue performance including Hell Let Loose and Bus Simulator franchises. The company maintains full-year consensus guidance of £175.3m revenues and £50.7m adjusted EBITDA, with results expected to be H2-weighted reflecting the rescheduled August 2026 launch of Hell Let Loose: Vietnam. Major H2 releases include Hell Let Loose: Vietnam, Bus Simulator 27, Wardogs, and Silver Pines, with Hell Let Loose: Vietnam showing strong pre-order momentum following successful playtesting.
17708239.brief: Everplay Group reiterates FY26 guidance of £175.3m revenue and £50.7m adjusted EBITDA, with H2-weighted delivery ahead of major game releases.
17708239.take: Positive signal: maintaining guidance despite competitive gaming market, backed by concrete H2 release schedule with encouraging pre-order indicators for flagship title, suggesting revenue confidence is well-founded.

17708256.summary: AIM-listed Flowtech delivered H1 2026 revenue of £70.4m (H1 2025: £56.9m), comprising 13.2% like-for-like growth plus contributions from recent acquisitions. All three geographic segments achieved market share gains. Five acquisitions (Thorite, Allswage, Thomas Group, Q Plus, Helipebs) are expected to contribute £30m annualised revenue and £3m+ annualised EBITDA for approximately £6m total consideration. Net debt reduced to £16.5m with £8.5m available headroom. Two major bridge infrastructure projects deferred to H2 2026. Full interim results announced 8 September 2026.
17708256.brief: Flowtech Fluidpower reports H1 2026 revenue up 23.7% to £70.4m, with 13.2% organic growth and successful acquisition integration.
17708256.take: Positive read: strong organic growth, successful M&A integration, reduced debt, and confidence in H2 performance despite macro headwinds and supply chain challenges positioned company well.

17708259.summary: Barclays delivered H1 2026 profit before tax of £6.1bn (up 17% YoY) with group return on tangible equity of 14.8% and earnings per share of 30.7p (up 24%). Group income reached £16.5bn (up 11%), with all divisions posting double-digit RoTE. The bank upgraded its 2026 total income target to approximately £31.5bn from £31bn and increased net interest income guidance. Capital distributions total £2.3bn (up 61% YoY), including a £1bn buyback and 5.9p dividend per share. CET1 ratio stands at 14.3%, within the 13-14% target range.
17708259.brief: Barclays posts strong H1 2026 results with 14.8% RoTE, upgrades 2026 income guidance, announces £2.3bn capital returns.
17708259.take: Strong earnings beat, upgraded guidance, and substantial shareholder returns likely support positive market reception; demonstrates resilience across business divisions and confidence in macroeconomic outlook.

17708215.summary: Journeo PLC (AIM: JNEO) achieved H1 2026 revenues of £37.6m, up 53% from £24.5m prior year, with adjusted profit before tax rising 10% to £3.0m. Cash fell to £12.6m following the £10.7m Crime and Fire Defence Systems acquisition in September 2025. Sales order intake increased 3% to £31m, while the opportunity pipeline more than doubled to £200m. Management expects full-year revenue marginally ahead of £72m consensus and adjusted PBT in line with £7.4m expectations.
17708215.brief: Journeo reports 53% revenue growth to £37.6m in H1 2026; full-year revenue guidance ahead of expectations.
17708215.take: Strong organic revenue growth and a substantially expanded pipeline suggest solid forward momentum, though margin expansion remains modest relative to the top-line surge, warranting investor focus on H2 execution.

17708216.summary: Gem Diamonds recovered 41,695 carats in H1 2026 versus 47,125 in H1 2025, reflecting lower Satellite Pipe contribution (48% decline). Despite 12% lower carat recovery, revenue jumped 33% to $59.5m as average price per carat rose 38% to $1,395, driven by strong demand for high-quality stones. Eight diamonds sold for over $1m each. A 346.99 carat 'Lesotho Jubilee' was recovered in June. CEO noted synthetic diamonds impact smaller stones, but Letšeng's premium positioning insulates it from broader market weakness.
17708216.brief: Gem Diamonds reports H1 2026 results tracking guidance; strong pricing offsets lower production volumes.
17708216.take: Strong pricing momentum and all metrics tracking 2026 guidance suggests operational stability and resilience despite synthetic diamond competition; likely viewed as modestly positive for a niche luxury producer.

17708217.summary: Gaming Realms expects H1 2026 group revenue of approximately £15.5m and adjusted EBITDA of £6.6m. Excluding non-core brand licensing (£0.7m vs £2.4m prior year), core revenue grew 9% and adjusted EBITDA rose 16% year-on-year. UK revenues increased 3% despite Remote Gaming Duty rising to 40% from 1 April 2026, with gross gaming revenue now exceeding pre-staking-limit levels. The group expanded into four new markets (Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya, Peru), released 11 new games, and launched in Alberta, Canada, bringing regulated market distribution to 33. Net cash stood at £13.5m after £6.0m returned via share buybacks.
17708217.brief: Gaming Realms reports H1 2026 revenue of £15.5m and adjusted EBITDA of £6.6m; core business grows 9% and 16% respectively despite UK tax headwinds.
17708217.take: Strong underlying operational growth and resilience in challenging UK regulatory environment, coupled with international expansion and positive cash generation, likely viewed positively by market; guidance reiterated for full-year targets.

17708218.summary: PCI-PAL's Annual Recurring Revenue grew 27% organically to £24.4m (FY25: £19.3m), with Contracted ARR up 24% to £27.5m, driven by new business momentum and strong customer retention at 96% Gross Revenue Retention. FY26 revenue estimated at £24.6m (up 9% YoY), ahead of market consensus of £23.7m, while Adjusted EBITDA expected at £1.1m versus consensus £0.85m. Company maintained £4.0m cash, debt-free, with strong momentum in US market and expanding partner ecosystem.
17708218.brief: PCI-PAL reports strong FY26 growth with ARR up 27% to £24.4m, beating market consensus on revenue and EBITDA.
17708218.take: Positive read: company beat consensus forecasts on near-term metrics while significantly growing forward-looking ARR/CARR indicators, signalling sustainable organic growth; deliberate investment strategy is yielding results.

17708219.summary: Johnson Service Group repurchased 1,276,675 ordinary shares between 20-24 July 2026 via Investec Bank under its May 2026 buyback programme. Prices ranged from 145.2p to 151.6p, with weighted average prices between 147.4p-150.1p daily. Total investment approximately £18.8m. All purchased shares will be cancelled, reducing share capital.
17708219.brief: JSG purchased 1.28m shares at 147-150p in week to 24 July as part of announced buyback; all shares to be cancelled.
17708219.take: Routine capital management executing pre-announced buyback at steady prices; no new information. Returns cash to remaining shareholders through reduced share count; generally neutral to mildly positive but market-expected.

17708220.summary: Primorus Investments PLC purchased 250,000 ordinary shares on 27 July 2026 at an average price of 3.44 pence per share on the LSE, totalling approximately £8,600. All repurchased shares are held in treasury. Post-transaction, the Company has 139.8m shares in issue with 15.6m treasury shares, resulting in 124.25m shares used for voting rights calculations.
17708220.brief: Primorus Investments repurchased 250,000 shares at 3.44p each, now holding 15.6m treasury shares.
17708220.take: Share buyback at modest scale typical of AIM companies; suggests management views valuation as attractive but signals no major capital allocation shift; routine shareholder capital management.

17708221.summary: Airtel Africa executed 1,477,898 ordinary share buybacks during 20-24 July 2026 at volume-weighted average prices ranging from 332.88p to 335.79p daily. Since the programme's May 2026 launch with Barclays Capital Securities, the company has repurchased 15,184,226 shares at 338.84p average. All purchased shares will be cancelled, reducing share count and potentially supporting earnings per share.
17708221.brief: Airtel Africa purchased 1.48m shares (20-24 July) at 332.8-335.5p; 15.2m shares bought since May at 338.84p average.
17708221.take: Routine capital management signalling confidence in valuation; buybacks at prices below the programme average (338.84p) are modestly positive. Market will likely view as non-event unless share accumulation accelerates materially.

17708224.summary: Empresaria (AIM: EMR) reports H1 FY2026 net fee income up ~5% despite challenging markets, with adjusted PBT rising approximately 250% year-on-year through improved margins and cost discipline. Full-year adjusted PBT now expected at least £5.2m, 27% ahead of market forecast. Net debt stable at £17.0m. Strong performance from IMS (Global Workforce Solutions) and Headway (Operational Outsourcing) divisions. Interim results due 26 August 2026.
17708224.brief: Empresaria trading update shows strong H1 growth; FY26 profit forecast 27% above consensus.
17708224.take: Significant profit upgrade significantly ahead of expectations signals strong operational execution and margin improvement; likely positive read given substantial beat to consensus, though modest revenue growth suggests gains primarily from cost control.

17708225.summary: On 27 July 2026, Gamma Communications purchased 16,419 ordinary shares via Investec at a weighted average price of 952.17p, with a daily range of 946.50p to 957.50p. Since the buyback programme commenced in January 2026, the company has acquired 2,827,466 shares and intends to cancel them. Post-settlement, Gamma will have 90,936,885 shares in issue, 1,503,674 treasury shares, and 89,433,211 voting rights. The company is in an offer period under Takeover Code Rule 2.9.
17708225.brief: Gamma Communications repurchases 16,419 shares at 946.50-957.50p under its buyback programme; total purchases now 2.83m shares.
17708225.take: Routine capital allocation activity during formal offer period; share buybacks typically signal management confidence but market reaction minimal given ongoing takeover process and regulatory constraints.

17708226.summary: VinaCapital Vietnam Opportunity Fund Limited repurchased 43,138 USD shares at GBP 4.141922 per share on 27 July 2026, to be held as treasury shares. Total treasury shares now stand at 6,836,819, with 120,242,704 shares in issue. Total voting rights in the Company are 120,242,704 as of 27 July 2026.
17708226.brief: VinaCapital Vietnam Opportunity Fund repurchased 43,138 shares at GBP 4.14 per share on 27 July 2026.
17708226.take: Routine share buyback disclosure with minimal market implications; standard capital management activity typical for closed-ended funds managing share price discount to NAV.

17708227.summary: Power Metal Resources (AIM: POW) has completed the first hole of its drilling programme on the eastern feeder dyke to the Molopo Farms Igneous Complex in southwestern Botswana. Hole 1-9 was drilled to 382m and intersected disseminated suspected nickel mineralisation within a leuconorite band between 243-269m downhole depth. Sampling and assaying are underway. The company holds 87.71% of Kalahari Key Mineral Exploration, which owns 100% of the project. The programme targets five high-interest geological targets across 1,600m of planned drilling.
17708227.brief: Power Metal Resources completes first drill hole at Molopo Farms in Botswana, intersecting suspected nickel mineralisation.
17708227.take: Early-stage positive signal for nickel-focused explorers; nickel mineralisation intersection validates targeting approach, though assay results are critical before meaningful conclusions. Encourages near-term news flow.

17708228.summary: Brown Advisory US Smaller Companies PLC purchased 10,000 of its own ordinary shares at 1606.5 pence per share on 28 July 2026 to be held in treasury. Following the transaction, issued share capital stands at 18,223,413 shares, with 7,196,206 held in treasury. For FCA disclosure purposes, the reporting figure is 11,027,207 shares in issue.
17708228.brief: Brown Advisory US Smaller Cos. repurchased 10,000 shares at 1606.5p per share for treasury.
17708228.take: Routine share buyback for treasury; modest transaction size suggests capital management activity rather than significant strategic signal to the market.

17708229.summary: Venture Life Group PLC purchased 152,860 ordinary shares on 27 July 2026 at 69.40 pence per share through Cavendish Capital Markets, holding them as treasury shares. Following the repurchase, the company has 128.86 million ordinary shares in issue with 8.28 million in treasury, reducing voting rights to 120.58 million shares. The buyback was conducted under the share repurchase programme announced 30 September 2025.
17708229.brief: Venture Life repurchases 152,860 shares at 69.40p per share under existing buyback programme.
17708229.take: Routine capital management activity under an established buyback programme; consistent with shareholder return objectives but offers no new information on trading performance or strategic direction.

17708214.summary: H1 2026 statutory revenue reached £11.6m, up 18% year-on-year (H1 2025: £9.8m), with organic growth of 9% excluding Southern Cross Diagnostics acquisition. Instrumentation segment grew 30%, Clinical segment 20%, driven by LightBench Discover platform and NIPT technology demand. All geographic regions showed growth: Americas >30%, Asia-Pacific 22%, EMEA 2%. SCD contributed £1.8m revenue from March completion. Cash declined to £8.9m from £19.1m (reflecting £5.5m SCD acquisition spend). Company expects £4m annualised cost savings from ongoing restructuring and raised €785k via subscription rights.
17708214.brief: Novacyt posts 18% H1 revenue growth to £11.6m, with strong momentum across all regions and segments.
17708214.take: Strong organic and acquisition-driven growth with momentum across all segments and regions supports positive sentiment, though cash burn concerns tempered by promised cost savings and cash runway extension.

17708212.summary: Between 20–24 July 2026, Fever-Tree Drinks purchased 183,581 ordinary shares (£0.0025 par) via Investec across XLON and AIMX venues.
